title: Is it a fair test? 1 block vs 3 blocks
about: Two identical red cars with the same clay roll down ramps that differ only in height: a fair test of ramp height.

source.question: Is this a valid experiment to test ramp height?
source.answer: Yes. The height is different, and everything else is the same.
words: Our question: does a higher ramp make a toy roll farther? We are testing ramp height.
Now both cars carry the same gray ball of clay.

story.says: What is new: both cars now carry the same gray clay.
The top ramp sits on 1 block, the bottom ramp on 3; the cars and the clay are the same.
Both cars roll down and onto the carpet.
Only the blocks differ: 1 under one ramp, 3 under the other; the same car and clay on each.

shots.intent: Open on what is new since the last part: from the two red cars ready on their ramps, push in on the gray clay on each roof (each band centred on its own car's clay, one scale), so the change is the first thing the child sees.

audit.question: Can a child see the same gray lump of clay on top of each red car?

shots.intent: Cut back to the two setups, one band each at one scale: the blocks under each ramp are the one thing that differs, labelled, with the same car and clay ready on top.

audit.question: Can a Grade 3 child count 1 block under the top ramp and 3 blocks under the bottom ramp?

shots.intent: As the gates lift, the camera stays with the pair and rides along beside them, one camera at one scale: both cars stay big as they roll down and onto the carpet. The question is about the setup, so two seconds of the roll are enough.

audit.question: Can a child see both red cars roll down their ramps and onto the carpet?

shots.intent: For the question, a fresh look at the setup, closer and from a little higher than the opening: each car with its clay on top of its ramp and the block stack under it, big and still. A new picture, not the opening again.

audit.question: Can a child see that the only difference between the two setups is 1 block against 3 blocks, with the same car and clay on each?

notes: Two runs (one per lane) share one camera at one scale. The question is about the setup, so the roll is short and close (a ride beside the pair), and the stop is a fresh, closer look at the setup rather than the opening picture again.
